title: A Mechanistic Analysis of Looped Reasoning Language Models
claim: Iterated blocks converge from a transient spiral onto a single stable cyclic trajectory, revealing fixed points in latent space.
layout: 2 side-by-side PCA plots, early vs late iterations, shared recurrence colorbar
description: Two square scatter-style line plots sit side by side, both with PC 1 on the x-axis and PC 2 on the y-axis, ranging from about -10 to 10 with dotted grid lines. The left panel, titled 'Recurrences 1-16', shows a thick polyline spiraling outward from a dark green start near the center to a bright yellow outer ring, with a small gap in the upper right. The right panel, titled 'Recurrences 17-32', shows a single tight closed loop, nearly all yellow with faint green edges, where successive recurrences overlap almost exactly. A vertical colorbar on the far right runs from dark green (Early) to yellow (Late), labeled 'Recurrence'. The eye goes first to the colorful spiral on the left, then to the clean ring on the right.
caption: Latent states after each block in a looped model frequently tend towards separate fixed points: a consistent trajectory in latent space. Illustrative; from a randomly initialized model.
abstract: Reasoning has become a central capability in large language models. Recent research has shown that reasoning performance can be improved by looping an LLM's layers in the latent dimension, resulting in looped reasoning language models. Despite promising results, few works have investigated how the internal dynamics and computation of looped models differ from that of standard feedforward models. In this paper, we conduct a mechanistic analysis of latent states and layer behavior in looped language models. We analyze cyclic recurrence and show that for many of the studied models each layer in the cycle converges to a distinct fixed point; consequently, the recurrent block follows a consistent cyclic trajectory in the latent space. We provide evidence that as these fixed points are reached, attention-head behavior stabilizes, leading to constant behavior - stages of inference - across recurrences. Empirically, we discover that recurrent blocks tend to organize their computation such that it closely mirrors that of feedforward models, repeating this behavior in depth with each iteration. We study how architectural choices influence the emergence and stability of these cyclic fixed points and stages of inference, providing practical guidance for looped language model design.
